metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.findings: The only discoverable artifacts are the language's own GitHub organization (quidra-lang) containing the core compiler repository and two first-party packages (dnn, vision), plus their release tags (v0.1.0 through v0.3.1, all created within days of each other in September 2026). No independent company, product, deployed service, job listing, or case study referencing production use of Quidra was found.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: This is a negative-evidence finding based on a single retrieval route (web search) at one snapshot time; it cannot rule out unpublished/private deployments, but the language's very recent creation date and single-organization repository structure make pre-existing production adoption evidence structurally unlikely to exist yet.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.predeclared_selection_rule: Search-engine-observable universe of production/deployment evidence for Quidra: case studies, company adoption announcements, job postings naming Quidra, conference talks, or public deployed-software references, retrieved via the same single web_search retrieval route used for the third-party tool metric.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.production_adoption_search_result: General web search for company/production adoption of quidra-lang returned no matching results; results were entirely unrelated (continuous-deployment methodology articles, unrelated 'Quill'/case-study documents). No production deployment, adopting organization, or real-world usage evidence exists in searchable public sources.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.rubric_basis: Per ecosystem.md, unsupported or absent ecosystem evidence intentionally covered by a metric receives the rubric-defined low score rather than N/A; production adoption/deployment evidence for Quidra is scored at the floor (0) because no independent deployment or adoption evidence was found.

citations.quote: A native programming language for humans and LLMs — less ceremony, less ambiguity, maximum meaning per token.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.findings: All discovered tooling for Quidra (compiler CLI, LSP server, built-in formatter, source-inspection/patch API, WebAssembly frontend bridge) is first-party, implemented inside the quidra-lang/quidra core repository itself, as described in the embedded architecture spec: the compiler ships its own LSP server, built-in formatter, and machine-readable 'describe' surfaces rather than relying on an external ecosystem.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Absence-of-evidence from search is not absolute proof no private/unindexed third-party tool exists, but Quidra is a newly created, single-organization benchmark language (releases v0.1.0-v0.3.1 all dated September 2026) with a 0-star/0-fork core repository per GitHub metadata, which is consistent with no independent tooling ecosystem having formed yet.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.predeclared_selection_rule: Search-engine-observable universe of independently authored (non quidra-lang-org) editor plugins, linters, formatters, CI actions, package-index tooling, or IDE integrations for the Quidra language, retrieved via provider web search (retrieval route: web_search tool, single route used identically for this language shard). Target candidates checked: (a) VS Code Marketplace / JetBrains Marketplace listings naming 'Quidra' or the '.qui' extension, (b) GitHub repositories outside the quidra-lang GitHub organization implementing Quidra tooling, (c) generic 'quidra-lang production deployment / third-party tool' web queries.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.rubric_basis: Per ecosystem.md, absent ecosystem evidence intentionally covered by a metric receives the rubric-defined low score rather than N/A; third-party tool availability for Quidra is scored at the floor (0) because no third-party (non first-party, non quidra-lang-authored) tool was found across the declared retrieval route.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.third_party_tool_search_result: The VS Code / JetBrains Marketplace and general web searches for Quidra-specific third-party editor plugins, linters, formatters, or CI integrations returned no matching listings. Results instead surfaced unrelated similarly-named projects (e.g. 'Quil', 'Quillscript', 'QML') and generic tooling documentation, confirming an absence of an externally observable third-party tool ecosystem for Quidra as of the snapshot time.
